doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Village, Big Sur and leaving the business
title: Frank Kofsky's book and refusing to fit a box
summary: Lloyd says the record company pitted him against Shepp, and he refused Frank Kofsky's book because he was not out yelling.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So anyway, he’s playin’... And so, that night... Oh actually Shep had some rivalry with me, cause it was the time... And the record company was pittin’ us against each other. There was a guy named Frank Kofsky, I don’t know if you ever ran into that name.

He was writing a book and he wanted me to be in it. He was writing on... and I was very high and very in the zone, and I called him on his stuff, you know, and he didn’t like it. I told him I was a spirit, I wasn’t gonna participate in what he was doing. See, they didn’t like me because I didn’t fit into a box, and I wasn’t just out there yellin’ on the thing. And I would go my own way.
